title: When a message can't be sent yet — the warning and its buttons

steps.path: Send a message while a permission card is still waiting for you
steps.headline: The warning now has a Show card button that takes you to the card that needs your answer.
steps.changed: Same sentence as before. A Show card button now sits before Send anyway; clicking it scrolls the chat to the waiting card and lights its edge up for a moment.
steps.notice: You no longer hunt for the card when it has scrolled out of view. Your typed message stays in the box either way.
steps.risk: If the card is very far up the chat, the app switches to terminal view instead, where the same question is waiting.

steps.path: Send a message while a Claude Code pop-up is open in terminal view (here: /status)
steps.headline: A pop-up open only in the terminal now stops the send, with an Open terminal button. Before, the message vanished.
steps.changed: Before this change there was no warning at all: the message looked sent but went into the pop-up and was lost. Captured in a dev window with real Claude Code.
steps.notice: Open terminal switches this chat to terminal view so you can answer or close the pop-up; Send anyway closes it and sends.
steps.risk: Send anyway presses Esc first, which cancels whatever the pop-up was asking.

steps.path: The warning above the message box when a send is refused
steps.headline: Are these the right words for each reason a message can't be sent yet?
steps.today: Two sentences exist now — "Your assistant is waiting for your response — answer the card in the chat first." (a permission or question card) and "… answer the prompt first." (a Claude Code menu shown as a card). Both have only Send anyway.
steps.problem: Three new situations need their own words: a pop-up only in the terminal, the agents list (where a message would start a NEW session), and history search.
steps.proposal: Card waiting: the two sentences above, plus Show card. Pop-up in the terminal: "Claude Code has something open in the terminal — answer or close it first." plus Open terminal. Agents list: "Claude Code's terminal is showing its agents list — anything sent there would start a new session. Press Esc in terminal view first." History search: "Claude Code's terminal is searching your past prompts — press Esc in terminal view first." If Send anyway cannot close it: "Claude Code didn't close it — switch to terminal view to answer it. Your message is still here."

options.label: Keep these words
pros: Each sentence says what is in the way and what to do.
The card sentences you already know stay the same.
cons: The agents-list and search sentences are long for a small bubble.

options.label: One short sentence
pros: Every warning reads the same: "Claude Code is waiting on something — answer it first."
cons: You lose the hint that a send from the agents list would start a new session.
The button is then the only clue to where to look.
